title: Mixed Team World Cup 2026 entry list: Calderano, Moregard and Lin Yun-Ju miss Chengdu as Russia join
seo_title: Mixed Team World Cup 2026: full entry list and format
description: Mixed Team World Cup 2026 entry list: 154 players from 20 teams in Chengdu, with Russia and Great Britain in and Calderano, Moregard and Lin Yun-Ju out.
standfirst: The ITTF's list for Chengdu has 154 players from 20 teams, including five who were not there last year, but three of the world's top seven men will not play.
body: Hugo Calderano, Truls Moregard and Lin Yun-Ju, three of the world's top seven men, are missing from the Mixed Team World Cup after the ITTF published the full entry list on Thursday: 154 players, 77 men and 77 women, from 20 teams for the event in Chengdu from 29 November to 6 December.

Russia, Poland, Slovakia, Singapore and Great Britain are all in a field that has grown from 16 teams to 20. None of the five played at last year's event, and Great Britain are appearing as one team for the first time. Europe has nine teams, Asia seven, the Americas two, and Africa and Oceania one each. China, who have won all three editions, play at home again, this time at the Chengdu High-tech Sports Center, which staged the World Team Championships Finals in 2022.
## Who is missing

Brazil's squad has no Calderano, the world No 7, and no Bruna Takahashi, the world No 29; Guilherme Teodoro, Leonardo Iizuka and Giulia Takahashi lead a team of four men and four women. Egypt are without Dina Meshref, the world No 30, and rely on Omar Assar and Hend Fathy. India have left out Manika Batra (No 63) and Sreeja Akula (No 67), so Diya Chitale, Syndrela Das, Yashaswini Ghorpade and Sutirtha Mukherjee make up the women's team. Batra was also named only as a reserve for the Asian Games, a decision that led India's leading players to [propose new selection rules](/news/india-players-selection-policy-proposal-manika-batra-ttfi-2026.html) this week. The ITTF's list gives no reasons for any of these absences.

Moregard is missing so that he can prepare for the WTT Finals in Hong Kong, as Eleven [reported](/news/mixed-team-world-cup-2026-sweden-squad-moregard-wtt-finals.html), and Germany's Dimitrij Ovtcharov [asked not to be picked](/news/mixed-team-world-cup-2026-germany-squad-winter-franziska-ovtcharov.html) after an upper-arm injury. Lin, the world No 5, is not on Taiwan's list, which has three men and four women. The Liberty Times reported that he withdrew on 11 November, [worried about the workload](/news/mixed-team-world-cup-2026-lin-yun-ju-cheng-i-ching-withdraw-taiwan-six-players.html) before the WTT Finals. The paper also reported that Cheng I-Ching withdrew a day later, but she is on the ITTF's list and its announcement names her as one of Taiwan's leaders.
## The favourites

China bring the world's top two women, Wang Manyu and Sun Yingsha, with Kuai Man (No 4) and Chen Yi (No 8), and a men's team of Wang Chuqin (No 4), Lin Shidong (No 10), Zhou Qihao (No 12) and Huang Youzheng. Their [squad](/news/mixed-team-world-cup-2026-china-squad-wang-chuqin-sun-yingsha-chen-yi-zhou-qihao.html) was named on 10 November.

Japan, last year's runners-up, have the world's top two men, Sora Matsushima and Tomokazu Harimoto, as well as Miwa Harimoto (No 3), Hina Hayata (No 6), Satsuki Odo, Honoka Hashimoto, Shunsuke Togami and Hiroto Shinozuka. South Korea, runners-up in 2023 and 2024, have named Jang Woojin (No 8), Lim Jonghoon, Oh Junsung and Park Ganghyeon, with Shin Yubin (No 13), Kim Nayeong, Lee Eunhye and Yoo Yerin. There is no place for An Jaehyun, the world No 37.
France have both Lebruns, Félix (No 3) and Alexis (No 9), with Simon Gauzy and Flavien Coton, while Germany, bronze medallists last year, are led by Sabine Winter and Patrick Franziska.
## The newcomers

Russia are led by Vladimir Sidorenko, the world No 17, and the European champion Elizabet Abraamian, No 26, with Nikita Artemenko, Evgeny Tikhonov, Denis Ivonin, Maria Panfilova, Mariia Tailakova and Vlada Voronina. Great Britain pick Tom Jarvis, Liam Pitchford, Connor Green and Samuel Walker, with Anna Hursey, Tin-Tin Ho, Tianer Yu and Charlotte Carey; Hursey, the world No 38, is the highest-ranked of the eight.

Poland have Natalia Bajor (No 41) and Milosz Redzimski, Singapore Izaac Quek and Zeng Jian, and Slovakia Wang Yang and Tatiana Kukulkova. Slovakia and Croatia have entered the minimum of three men and three women. Chile, who played last year, are the first reserves.
## How it works

The 20 teams are split into two groups of 10 and each team plays everyone in its group. The ITTF places the top seeds in Group 1 and the second seeds in Group 2, then draws the rest into the groups two at a time in seeding order, using a seeding list it publishes this month.

Each tie opens with mixed doubles, followed by men's and women's singles, in an order decided by a toss, and then men's and women's doubles. Every match is best of three games and the first team to win eight games takes the tie, so later matches can stop after one or two games. A player can play at most two matches in a tie. A win is worth two points and a defeat one.

After the group stage, the top two in each group go into the semi-finals, third and fourth play for fifth to eighth places, and so on down to seventh and eighth, who play for 13th to 16th. The bottom two in each group finish joint 17th. There will be 106 ties in all.
## Schedule (UK time)
- Sunday 29 November: opening ceremony 2am, first group ties from 3am, evening session from 9.30am
- Monday 30 November to Friday 4 December: group stage, sessions from 2am and 9.30am
- Saturday 5 December: semi-finals at 3.30am and 10am, with the placing ties
- Sunday 6 December: third-place tie 5.30am, final midday

Times are approximate and Chengdu is eight hours ahead of the UK. The final is two days before the WTT Finals start in Hong Kong on 8 December. Eleven's [event page](/events/mixed-team-world-cup-2026.html) has every squad, and will have the groups, the schedule and live scores once the draw is made.
